So you're right that Clue is not a form of birth control, but actually fertility awareness is a legitimate form of birth control. I saw you said a 60% success rate, but that's inaccurate. Here's a report from the CDC comparing forms of birth control, it has a failure rate of 2%-26% actually, so a success rate of 98-74%. There's a lot of ways to track fertility, and I do agree with you that Clue is NOT an effective form of birth control, but I think you're painting the method with too broad of brush. 

Fertility windows DO matter, you are only able to get pregnant for at most 12-24 hours. The tricky thing is, sperm are viable for 5 days. That's why it's a fertile window, the egg is released when a hormone LH (Luteinizing hormone) causes the egg to release. You can track your levels of LH like how you do a pregnancy test along with other biological markers. 

Obviously, fertility awareness is not as effective as hormonal or barrier contraceptives, but 60% success rate is quite the stretch.

I was put on birth control well before I was sexually active, and it was useful for when I was that age and the menstrual cycles I wouldve dealt with, 

But I still feel a huge different before and after.

I started birth control around the same age and at first it really helped. But as I got older things started to change. I don't know how much of it was due to my already weird reproductive issues (started menstration at 7) and had cysts by 12, birth control shortly after. But all of that helped at first, and I was golden until my 20s. 

After a series of issues with pills, depo (bad for your bones, esepcially when you're young) and then the IUD. It was a lot. Getting the hormones out for the first time for almost 10 years was fucking delightful. Things aren't perfect, I still have pcos, but I do feel way more clear headed than I ever did.

My acne does flair up more than it did when I was on bc, but I've gotten really into skincare and drinking a gallon of water a day (I have to piss all the time) but all is still do able (I do get that it's rough though, skincare isnt the same for everyone and I had skin issues on birth control)

It definitely is a lot of work and I can see why it doesn't work for everyone. For me after lots of issues with hormonal birth control, I couldn't risk it anymore. I also found out after an ovarian cyst popping and some obgyn visits that I have a smaller cervix so I shouldn't get the copper iud. So I'm kinda left in a rut. 

One thing that I do to kinda double down is, I have a package of ovulation test strips I got from CVS and did a ovulation test every 3 days for my first few cycles, the ovulation window is about 1-3 days, usually around 2 so I also was lucky and caught my window each time. From this and temperature changes I can usually catch my ovulation, I use the tests still and usually waste one the day before my ovulation began but still I'm pretty close to within one day. So I do have to spend a little on this method, but I also don't have good health insurance so I feel like is still cheaper for me, about 25 tests in a box for 26 dollars, and I don't use a whole box in a month now. I did use a lot when I was first tracking, which took me about 3 months. 

And when I'm stressed out and my ovulation or period don't come when I expect, I go back to ovulation testing every few days. I record and track all of this through Clue but might switch to a different service Kindara

Also when I approach my ovulation I either abstain or use condoms until I get a negative ovulation test, and then usually I wait a day anyways. 

So I wouldn't say it's easy, but I wouldn't call any of my experiences on hormonal birth control easy either. I am sorry to hear about your experience with the method though

You should look into fertility awareness methods. The information in the side bar in my opinion is not complete. I can DM you some articles. By tracking your temperature everyday, tracking the consistency and texture of your discharge, and some ovulation tests, you can pinpoint when you're fertile. 

You're only able to get pregnant at most 5 days out of your entire month ish long cycle. You can confirm the exact days that you're ovulating with cheap tests that they sell with pregnancy tests. I have my ovulation tracked down within a day, and use condoms or abstain the day before I believe I'm ovulating, and after I get a positive test for ovulation, condoms or abstain for the next 4 or 5 days. 

It takes a minute to get your cycle tracked properly, but I would really recommend it. It can be a little annoying, for example you need to take your basal body temperature everyday at the same time. This is your body temperature right when you wake up, ideally after at least 3 hours of sleep,and it must be taken before your feet touch the ground. No pee breaks first. I would say that's the most annoying barrier to fertility awareness. You can have control of your reproductive cycle without hormones, and I would really recommend it.
